hook.head: Field File 23 · Along the Railroad
rows: An old town from the days when railroads were new
Your teacher, still stuck inside Canvas
hook.alt: An old photo of a woman at the front of a long line of girls in white dresses
hook.cap: Mary McLeod Bethune and her students, Daytona, 1905. State Archives of Florida.
hook.note: One person's choices can change a whole state. Visit an old railroad town for me, then tell me about one person who changed Florida.

opti.brief: She can't leave Canvas, so you go. Scout an old town in VR and send her one short video.
opti.desk: No headset? Use my desk. Play the game, then write 2 sentences for your teacher.

vr.look: This map is an old town in the American West, from the time when railroads were new. Florida towns grew the same way when Henry Flagler's and Henry Plant's railroads reached them.

place.alt: A crowd of people beside a train
place.html: Railroads made towns grow: Flagler's railroad reached Miami in 1896 and Key West in 1912.
place.cap: The first train reaches Key West, January 22, 1912. Library of Congress.

say: One person who changed Florida is ___, because ___.

steps.title: Get ready
steps.html:
@PLACE@

In your video, you say these 2 sentences:

@SAY@

Practice now. Say both before the timer ends.

@TIMER@

In VR, this page is on the Canvas tab.

steps.title: Go in
steps.html:
🔗 First time only: connect Canvas at xr.optimaed.com. See Having trouble in VR? below.

Open the On-Demand app. Click Explore. Type Western in Filter environments. Click Western Town, then Begin Solo.

steps.title: Scout the town
steps.html: Move with the thumbstick. Walk along the main street. Stop where you can see the buildings up close.

steps.title: Record your video and send it
steps.html:
Open your menu, click Library, then Camera. Fit the street in the tablet. Click Record video, say your 2 sentences, and click it again to stop.

On the Canvas tab, pick @CANVAS@. Click Choose from My Files, pick your video, click Use this file, then Submit to Canvas. Look for the green Submitted tag.

🔁 To fix it, send a new video.

steps.title: Check and leave
steps.html: Press the Meta button, then click Quit. Check that your video is in the Canvas assignment. Not there? See Having trouble in VR?

extra.html: If you see train tracks, stand near them while you record.

vr.full: One video, 30 seconds or less, showing the place while you say both sentences.

studio.title: Who Am I?
studio.look: Six people who shaped Florida. Each round gives clues about one of them.
studio.do: Read the clues. Tap the person they describe.

game.miss: Not this person. Read all the clues again.
game.done: You named all six! Each one made a choice that changed Florida.

rounds.gave: A railroad all the way to Key West
rounds.ok: Yes! Henry Flagler's train reached Key West in 1912.
clues: I was a business partner of John D. Rockefeller.
My railroad reached Key West in 1912, when I was 82.

rounds.gave: A school that became Bethune-Cookman University
rounds.ok: Yes! Mary McLeod Bethune started her school in 1904.
clues: In 1904 I started a school with $1.50 and five girls.

rounds.ok: Yes! Julia Tuttle is called the Mother of Miami.
clues: I owned land along the Miami River.
After the freezes of 1894 and 1895, I offered Flagler free land.

rounds.gave: Ybor City, the cigar capital of the world
rounds.ok: Yes! Vicente Martinez Ybor built Ybor City in Tampa.
clues: In 1885 I moved my cigar business to Tampa.
I built a company town for my workers.

rounds.gave: A railroad to Tampa and the Tampa Bay Hotel
rounds.ok: Yes! Henry Plant built up Florida's west coast.
clues: My railroad linked Tampa to markets up north.
I built the grand Tampa Bay Hotel.

rounds.ok: Yes! Marjory Stoneman Douglas called it a River of Grass.
clues: My 1947 book called the Everglades a River of Grass.
I lived to be 108 and never stopped speaking up.
